content.text:
The drawing shows a benzene ring carrying three substituents.

- A carboxamide group, C(=O)NH2, is attached at the upper right of the ring.
- A chlorine is attached at the bottom of the ring, on the carbon adjacent to the amide-bearing carbon (ortho).
- A nitro group, O2N, is attached at the upper left. Counting around the ring from the amide carbon (C1), the chlorine is on C2 and the nitro is on C5.

That makes the compound 2-chloro-5-nitrobenzamide.

As a SMILES string: NC(=O)c1cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc1Cl

Atom check: the ring carbons are c1 (bearing the amide), c (H), c (bearing NO2), c (H), c (H) and c1 (bearing Cl). The nitro carbon is therefore meta to the amide carbon, which is position 5, and the Cl carbon is ortho to it, which is position 2. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: NC(=O)c1cc([N+](=O)[O-])ccc1Cl
